diagnosis: The per-group global-consistency scorer does not identify cells. The true planted value is CONSISTENT (v1 median support 1.00: it beats a random background at every occurrence) but not DISTINCTIVE: many wrong values are equally consistent, and no aggregation tried (support, mean margin, strong background, tier-clean bigrams) separates them (best MRR 0.217 < 0.30 bar; best top-1 0.091 = 8.1x chance but MRR collapses). Root causes, all confirmed in the control detail: (1) French bigram contexts underdetermine a cell — for single letters, the letter-bigram model cannot distinguish the true letter from other common letters (common-letter attractors s/t/d/l win); (2) the tier-crossing approximation scores SYL candidates via edge letters, so single-letter impostors matching a true edge (s for les) outscore the truth; (3) restricting to clean SYL-SYL bigrams starves the scorer (26/40 groups drop below 8 informative occurrences with 7 anchors); (4) support saturates under a weak null and collapses under a strong null — the bigram likelihood P(context|v) is not discriminative, so no per-occurrence aggregation can fix it. The missing ingredient is JOINT inference: single-letter cells come in split pairs (d|e from de), and syllable identity needs syllable-level neighbors — both require assigning multiple groups simultaneously (EM / annealing over the full substitution key), not per-group scoring.
real_drag_note: NOT RUN: control gate failed for all three variants (WO3 control-first rule).
best_next_step: Abandon per-group scoring for cell identification. The validated direction is joint decipherment: simulated annealing / EM over the full 96-group substitution key maximizing global bigram likelihood under the two-tier cell model, with the 7 anchors pinned and split-pair structure (letter cells emitted in adjacent pairs) as a structural prior. Validate any such solver on the same synthetic control (planted mapping recovery, top-1/MRR vs chance) before touching R5005.
